reading.title: A Fictional Election
reading.text: In the republic of Valmar, the people hold a general election every four years. This year the government called an election earlier than planned because it could not agree on a new tax. During the election campaign, the leaders of the two main parties visited towns and villages. One of them promised to improve local government and build more libraries. The other said that government policy on transport must change. On election day, millions of citizens went to the polls. The party led by Mrs Dorin won the election, and she began to form a government the next week.

reading.title: The School Council Vote
reading.text: Last Friday our school held a vote to choose a new head of the school council. Three students stood for the job. Every pupil had the right to vote, and the voting was secret. We went to the polling station, which was just the library, and each of us cast one vote. The teachers counted the papers after lunch. A girl named Mira won the vote with sixty votes. She promised to talk about the canteen menu at the first meeting. Some pupils voted against her, but they all clapped when the result was announced.

reading.title: Helping Our Society
reading.text: Our teacher says that school is a small society. Everyone is a member, and everyone has a role. Last month our class started a charity society to help older people in our street. We bring them food and read to them. Our teacher explained that a fair society looks after all its members, not only the strong ones. She also told us that modern society faces many social problems, such as loneliness and poverty. Small actions can benefit society as a whole, she said. We agreed, and now more pupils want to join us.

reading.title: A Question of Justice
reading.text: Last year, a boy in our town was blamed for breaking a shop window. He said he was innocent, but nobody listened. His older sister had a strong sense of justice and decided to find the truth. She looked at the shop's camera pictures and showed them to the police. They saw that the real person was a stranger, and they brought him to justice. The boy was free, and the shop owner said sorry. The judge said it could have been a miscarriage of justice, and he thanked the sister. Now she wants to study law and work in the justice system.

listening.title: Justice for Everyone
listening.script: Teacher: Today we are talking about justice. What does the word mean to you? Pupil: For me, it means fair treatment. A just decision is one that does not take a side. Teacher: Good. Can you give an example? Pupil: Yes. If two pupils break a rule, both should get the same punishment. That is equal justice. Teacher: Excellent. Remember that a good justice system also listens to everyone before it decides.

reading.title: New Laws in Our City
reading.text: Our city council has introduced two new laws this year. The first law is about bicycles. By law, every cyclist under sixteen must wear a helmet. The second law is against dropping litter in parks. People who break the law must pay a small fine. The police enforce both rules, but they also explain them to visitors. Our mayor said that most people in the city are law-abiding and want a clean, safe place to live. My sister now wants to study law because she wants to help write fair rules one day.
